title: Choose the visual world for react-ui-kit v2
question: The roll assigned Vägmärke (Swedish road signs). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Vägmärke
options.lineage: Swedish road signs: yellow warning triangles, blue direction signs, Tratex lettering
options.thesis: Every state reads like a road sign: once, at speed, without doubt.
options.viewport: A yellow sign-gantry header over a white work area; stats as big road-sign numerals; the next task signed like a direction sign with its distance.
options.risk: Yellow shell can feel loud in long sessions; dark theme must become night-time reflective, not a recolour.

raised.raise: Every record (word, card, row, person) carries one fixed identity plate in the same place everywhere.
Every set of charts or sparklines in one view shares one scale and one baseline.
Nothing is labelled twice: one label per fact, no echo captions.

options.label: Monteringsanvisning
options.lineage: flat-pack assembly sheets: numbered steps, line diagrams, counts like 1×
options.thesis: Every flow is an assembly sheet: numbered steps, one action each, pictures before words.
options.viewport: White sheet with a black line-art rail; the session as numbered step panels with large step numerals and one diagram each.
options.risk: Scandinavian-instructions is a familiar trope, and line-art diagrams cost authoring time per app.

options.label: Graphite console
options.thesis: A graphite working surface, panels split by one-pixel seams, colour only for state.
options.viewport: Persistent panel layout; navigation swaps panel contents; destructive actions isolated by space.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for dashboards and admin; weak for learners, games and landing pages.
options.risk: Near-black with syntax accents is itself a common generated look.

options.label: Terminal yellow
options.thesis: Every screen shows only the next decision, signed like an airport junction.
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band naming the next decision and its time; the rest of the screen quiet and white.
options.case: Strong clarity for multi-step apps; overlaps the assigned sign world but is international rather than Swedish.
options.risk: Yellow bands everywhere tire in long sessions; wayfinding costume on dashboards.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: Live numbers flip into place like a departure board; everything else holds still.
options.viewport: Ruled board of rows; streak, due count and timers flip character by character when they change.
options.case: Gives the system its most memorable motion for stats, timers and scores; thin for forms and long reading.
options.risk: Novelty if every number flips; must be limited to genuinely live values.

options.label: Character catalog
options.thesis: A ranked roster of rounded mascots, each with fixed personal furniture.
options.viewport: Pastel grid of ranked characters with name plates.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dashboards, admin and payments do not read as a mascot roster.
options.kept: Every entity carries the same fixed furniture in the same place.

options.label: Botanical folio
options.thesis: One subject followed through stages at one exact scale.
options.viewport: Five fixed-scale plates on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses poorly and lands on cream plus serif, the generated default we are leaving.
options.kept: Comparisons share one exact scale and baseline.

options.label: Catalog sleeve
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry; labels are coded colour strips.
options.viewport: A single pulse plot on black with a catalog number.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels fight the accessibility floor and task clarity.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS dashboard: white ground, rounded cards, one blue accent, Inter.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, card grid of KPIs, table below, executed with full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other generated app by design.
